diagnostics.$comment: Authoritative catalog of JuLC compiler diagnostics. Each entry has a stable JULC#### code, a generated Java constant, an emitted-message template, a one-line root cause, a canonical fix snippet, and optionally example bad/good code. Consumed by: (1) generated DiagnosticCodes.java, (2) the MCP julc_explain_diagnostic tool, (3) docs/AI catalog resources, (4) future full compiler diagnostic coverage tests.

categories.SYNTAX: Java syntax forms not supported in the on-chain subset
categories.STDLIB: Stdlib method usage errors (wrong arity, missing args)

diagnostics.title: Method must have a body
diagnostics.summary: An abstract or interface method was found where the compiler expects a concrete method body. On-chain code cannot contain abstract methods.
diagnostics.fix: Provide a body for every method in your validator class.

diagnostics.title: Variable must be initialized
diagnostics.summary: A local variable was declared without an initializer. UPLC has no notion of uninitialized state.
diagnostics.fix: Initialize at declaration, e.g. `var x = BigInteger.ZERO;`. Re-bind via a new `var` if you need a different value later (UPLC is single-assignment).

diagnostics.title: Cannot return inside while loop
diagnostics.summary: `return` statements are not allowed inside `while` loops. UPLC `while` is desugared to a fixed-point `LetRec` that needs an explicit accumulator.
diagnostics.fix: Use a boolean accumulator and return after the loop. `break` works inside `for-each` if you only need early termination.

diagnostics.title: break statement outside of a loop
diagnostics.template: break statement outside of a loop
diagnostics.summary: `break` was used outside of a `for-each` or `while` loop body.
diagnostics.fix: Place the `break` inside a loop, or refactor to use early `return` from a helper method.

diagnostics.title: Switch is not exhaustive on sealed interface
diagnostics.template: Switch on sealed interface {0} is not exhaustive. Missing cases: {1}
diagnostics.summary: A `switch` expression on a sealed interface is missing one or more permitted variants.
diagnostics.fix: Add the missing case branches or include a `default ->` branch to handle all remaining variants.

diagnostics.title: Method does not return on all paths
diagnostics.template: Method {0} may not return a value on all execution paths
diagnostics.summary: A non-void method has at least one execution path that does not return a value.
diagnostics.fix: Ensure every if/else branch returns, or add a fallthrough return at the end of the method.

diagnostics.title: Switch expression requires a sealed interface type
diagnostics.template: switch expression requires a sealed interface type, got: {0}
diagnostics.summary: `switch` was used on a non-sealed type. Records (including `Tuple2`/`Tuple3`) cannot be switched on.
diagnostics.fix: Use field access (`pair.first()`, `pair.second()`) for records. Reserve `switch` for sealed interfaces with permitted record variants.

diagnostics.title: @Entrypoint method has wrong parameter count
diagnostics.template: {0} entrypoint must have {1} parameters{2}, found {3} in {4}.{5}(){6}
diagnostics.summary: The @Entrypoint method's parameter count doesn't match the validator kind. SpendingValidator entrypoints take 2 or 3 params (datum, redeemer, ctx); other validators take 2 (redeemer, ctx).
diagnostics.fix: Adjust the entrypoint signature to match the validator annotation. Spending: `(Datum, Redeemer, ScriptContext)`. Others: `(Redeemer, ScriptContext)`.

diagnostics.title: No @Entrypoint method found
diagnostics.summary: The validator class has no method annotated `@Entrypoint`.
diagnostics.fix: Annotate exactly one `public static` method with `@Entrypoint`. The method must return `boolean` (or `void` for newer signature shapes).

diagnostics.title: No validator annotation found
diagnostics.summary: The class has no validator annotation. Expected one of @SpendingValidator, @MintingValidator, @CertifyingValidator, @WithdrawValidator, @VotingValidator, @ProposingValidator (or @MultiValidator).
diagnostics.fix: Add the appropriate validator annotation at the class level.

diagnostics.title: Undefined variable
diagnostics.summary: A variable was referenced that is not in scope. Most commonly: typo, used before declared, or shadowed inside a switch case binding.
diagnostics.fix: Check spelling and declaration order. If a switch case binds a field with the same name as your method parameter, rename one of them — the field shadows the parameter inside the case body (see JULC0021).

diagnostics.title: Cannot resolve type
diagnostics.summary: The compiler could not resolve a type reference. The class may not be on the classpath, may not be a registered ledger/stdlib type, or may not be a valid on-chain type.
diagnostics.fix: Ensure the type is imported and is one of: a record, sealed interface, ledger type, JulcList/JulcMap/Optional/Tuple, or primitive (BigInteger, byte[], boolean, String).

diagnostics.title: Banned @Param type
diagnostics.template: @Param type ''{0}'' is not allowed. @Param values are always raw Data at runtime; using a typed Data subtype causes the compiler to misinterpret the runtime representation.
diagnostics.summary: @Param fields cannot be raw `PlutusData` subtypes (`PlutusData.BytesData`, `PlutusData.MapData`, `PlutusData.ListData`, `PlutusData.IntData`) — these confuse the parameter wrapping pipeline.
diagnostics.fix: Use byte[], BigInteger, typed records, redeemers, or @Param PlutusData only for opaque data.

diagnostics.title: Arrays are not supported (except byte[])
diagnostics.summary: Java arrays other than `byte[]` are not supported on-chain.
diagnostics.fix: Use `JulcList<T>` or `List<T>` instead of `T[]`.

diagnostics.title: try/catch is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: UPLC has no exception model — only `error` (immediate script failure).
diagnostics.fix: Use if/else checks instead of exception handling

diagnostics.title: throw is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: There is no exception machinery in UPLC.
diagnostics.fix: Return false from the validator to reject a transaction

diagnostics.title: null is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: There is no `null` value in the on-chain type system.
diagnostics.fix: Use Optional<T> (Optional.of(x) / Optional.empty()) to represent absence of a value

diagnostics.title: C-style for loops are not supported
diagnostics.template: C-style for loops are not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: Only `for-each` (`for (var x : list)`) and `while` loops are supported on-chain.
diagnostics.fix: Use for-each over a list or while loops instead

diagnostics.title: do-while loops are not supported
diagnostics.template: do-while loops are not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: Do-while is not supported on-chain.
diagnostics.fix: Use while loops or for-each instead

diagnostics.title: Floating-point types are not supported
diagnostics.template: floating point types (float/double) are not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: `float` and `double` have no UPLC equivalent.
diagnostics.fix: Use `BigInteger` for integer math. For fractional values, scale up (e.g. parts-per-million) and do integer math, or use `Rational` from the ledger types when modelling protocol params.

diagnostics.title: Switch case field name shadows method parameter
diagnostics.template: Switch case binding name shadows a method parameter
diagnostics.summary: When a sealed-interface variant has a field with the same name as a method parameter, the field binding silently shadows the parameter inside the switch case body. The compiler may not always catch this — be vigilant.
diagnostics.fix: Always use distinct names. Example: rename `time` parameter to `point` when switching on `IntervalBoundType.Finite(time)`.

diagnostics.title: Lambda cannot be stored in a variable
diagnostics.template: Lambda cannot be stored in a variable
diagnostics.summary: Lambdas must be passed inline as arguments to higher-order functions. Storing a lambda in a `Function<X,Y>` variable and calling `.apply(...)` is not supported.
diagnostics.fix: Pass the lambda directly: `list.map(x -> ...)`, `list.filter(p -> ...)`. If you need to share lambda logic, extract it as a regular static method (not as a lambda).

diagnostics.title: Mutually recursive bindings with more than 2 participants not supported
diagnostics.template: Mutually recursive bindings with more than 2 participants not yet supported: {0}
diagnostics.summary: JuLC supports self-recursion and mutual recursion between exactly 2 helpers (via Bekic's theorem). Three or more mutually recursive functions are not supported.
diagnostics.fix: Refactor: combine the helpers into a single function with an accumulator, or break the recursion via an explicit dispatch on a sealed interface.

diagnostics.title: Unknown method on type
diagnostics.summary: A method was called that doesn't exist on the receiver type. Likely the AI invented a method that isn't in the stdlib.
diagnostics.fix: Check the stdlib catalog at https://julc.dev/ai/catalog.json or the stdlib reference at https://julc.dev/stdlib/stdlib-guide/. Common: `JulcList<T>` has `head/tail/get/size/isEmpty/contains/prepend/reverse/concat/take/drop/map/filter/any/all/find`.

diagnostics.title: Stdlib method called with wrong number of arguments
diagnostics.template: Stdlib method called with wrong number of arguments: {0}
diagnostics.summary: A stdlib method was called with the wrong arity. Examples: `list.map()` requires a function argument, `list.contains()` requires an element argument, `map.insert()` requires (key, value).
diagnostics.fix: See the message itself — it includes a `Usage:` hint with the correct signature.

diagnostics.title: @NewType requires exactly one field
diagnostics.template: @NewType record {0} must have exactly one field
diagnostics.summary: @NewType is a single-field record wrapper around a primitive (byte[], BigInteger, String, boolean). Multi-field @NewType records are not allowed.
diagnostics.fix: Reduce to one field, or remove @NewType and use a plain record (which compiles to ConstrData).

diagnostics.title: Unsupported @NewType field type
diagnostics.summary: @NewType's underlying field must be a primitive: `byte[]`, `BigInteger`, `String`, or `boolean`.
diagnostics.fix: Change the underlying field to a supported primitive, or remove @NewType.

diagnostics.title: Failed to parse source
diagnostics.summary: The Java source could not be parsed. Usually a syntax error in the source file.
diagnostics.fix: Check the file with a Java IDE or `javac` — the JuLC compiler relies on JavaParser to produce a clean AST.

diagnostics.title: Duplicate record / sealed interface type
diagnostics.summary: Two different declarations registered the same type name.
diagnostics.fix: Rename one of the types, or ensure they are not both on the compilation classpath.

diagnostics.title: Circular type dependency detected
diagnostics.summary: Type registration found a cycle that cannot be resolved.
diagnostics.fix: Break the cycle by introducing a parameterized record or refactoring the involved types.

examples.$comment: Tagged index of julc-examples for AI agent retrieval. Each entry has stable metadata that the future MCP julc_examples_search tool can query: difficulty, concepts, cipRelevance, kind, and optional canonical. Examples flagged canonical:true are the recommended first-look set for an AI agent learning JuLC — idiomatic patterns covering the breadth of validators, minting policies, sealed-interface redeemers, HOFs, and on-chain libraries. Source files are paths within this repo.

concepts.parameterized-validator: Uses @Param fields baked in at compile time
concepts.sealed-interface-redeemer: Redeemer is a sealed interface with multiple permitted record variants, dispatched via switch
concepts.multi-sig: Validates multiple signatures in the transaction signatories list
concepts.datum-state-transition: Spending validator that checks an output datum reflects an updated state from the input datum
concepts.value-arithmetic: Uses ValuesLib add/subtract/eq/leq/geq for multi-asset value comparison
concepts.interval-deadline: Uses IntervalLib.contains for time-based deadline enforcement
concepts.hof-lambda: Uses higher-order functions (list.map / filter / any / all / find / foldl) with inline lambdas
concepts.for-each-loop: Uses for-each over JulcList<T> or JulcMap<K,V>
concepts.while-loop: Uses while loop with explicit accumulator
concepts.nested-loops: Loops within loops (outer for-each / while + inner)
concepts.onchain-library: Uses or defines a @OnchainLibrary helper class
concepts.onchain-library-shared: Demonstrates sharing a library across multiple validators
concepts.address-credential-switch: Switches on Credential / sealed-interface to filter by credential type
concepts.linked-list: On-chain linked-list pattern (head pointer + next pointer datums)
concepts.atomic-swap: Atomic swap pattern between two parties
concepts.payment-splitter: Splits an incoming payment across multiple recipients
concepts.factory: Factory pattern that mints child scripts/tokens
concepts.one-shot-mint: Single-mint policy bound to a specific UTxO
concepts.raw-plutusdata-interop: Uses raw PlutusData for interop (acceptable case, not anti-pattern)
concepts.wingriders-benchmark: Real-world DEX validator used for performance benchmarking
concepts.multi-validator: Uses @MultiValidator to combine multiple purposes (mint + spend etc.) in one script class
concepts.optional-type: Uses Optional<T> for nullable / maybe-absent values
concepts.output-datum-switch: Switches on the OutputDatum sealed interface (NoOutputDatum/OutputDatumHash/InlineDatum)
concepts.inline-datum: Reads metadata or state from an InlineDatum on a UTxO
concepts.signatory-check: Verifies that specific PubKeyHashes appear in TxInfo.signatories()
concepts.script-context-fields: Reads multiple fields off ScriptContext / TxInfo / ScriptInfo (typed access, not raw PlutusData)
concepts.value-singleton: Constructs a single-asset Value via Value.singleton or Value.lovelace
concepts.policy-id-token-name: Manipulates PolicyId / TokenName newtype wrappers explicitly

examples.name: VestingValidator
examples.title: Time-locked vesting
examples.summary: Spending validator that releases funds to a beneficiary. Demonstrates typed datum/redeemer records and signatory checks.

examples.name: EscrowValidator
examples.title: Buyer-seller escrow with refund
examples.summary: Two-party escrow with both a complete path (buyer + seller signatures + payment) and a refund path (seller signature + past deadline). Reuses ValidationUtils @OnchainLibrary helpers.

examples.name: AuctionValidator
examples.title: Auction with sealed-interface redeemer
examples.summary: Two-variant sealed interface redeemer (Bid / Close) dispatched via switch expression. Different field counts per variant.

examples.name: MultiSigTreasury
examples.title: 2-of-N multi-signature treasury
examples.summary: Spending validator requiring two distinct signers from the datum.

examples.name: MultiSigMinting
examples.title: Multi-action minting policy
examples.summary: Three-variant sealed interface redeemer (MintByAuthority / BurnByOwner / MintByMultiSig). Demonstrates @MintingValidator with no datum.

examples.name: OneShotMintPolicy
examples.title: One-shot UTxO-bound minting
examples.summary: Parameterized minting policy that can only mint when a specific UTxO is consumed. The canonical pattern for unique NFTs.

examples.name: GuardedMinting
examples.title: Authority-guarded minting
examples.summary: Minting policy that requires a parameterized authority signature.

examples.name: OutputCheckValidator
examples.title: Minimum payment to recipient
examples.summary: Demonstrates OutputLib usage: lovelacePaidTo, countOutputsAt. Datum stores a typed Address.

examples.name: WhitelistTreasuryValidator
examples.title: Whitelist-restricted treasury
examples.summary: Spending validator that only allows whitelisted signers to spend, using a list-membership check.

examples.name: TokenDistributionValidator
examples.title: Multi-beneficiary distribution with HOFs
examples.summary: Treasury that distributes tokens to a list of beneficiaries. Showcases higher-order functions: list.all, list.any, list.filter with lambda variable capture and block bodies. Sealed interface redeemer (Distribute / Cancel). Switches on Credential.

examples.name: MpfRegistryValidator
examples.title: Merkle Patricia Forestry registry
examples.summary: Registry validator using Merkle Patricia Forestry for compact on-chain set membership. Uses self-recursive helpers and the MPF library.

examples.name: MerklePatriciaForestry
examples.title: Merkle Patricia Forestry verification library
examples.summary: @OnchainLibrary providing MPF proof verification primitives. Used by MpfRegistryValidator. Demonstrates self-recursive UPLC compilation.

examples.name: Cip68Nft
examples.title: CIP-68 NFT with on-chain metadata
examples.summary: CIP-68 multi-validator with a reference NFT (label 100) carrying inline-datum metadata and a user NFT (label 222). Demonstrates @MultiValidator (MINT + SPEND), parameterized validator, two sealed-interface redeemers, OutputDatum switch, Credential switch, and HOF lambda with block body.

examples.name: LinkedListValidator
examples.title: On-chain linked list pattern
examples.summary: Demonstrates the on-chain linked list pattern used to represent unbounded sets of UTxOs (head/tail pointers in datums). Note: uses raw PlutusData casts for the linked-list manipulation — advanced pattern, not the recommended idiom for new code.

examples.name: LinkedListLib
examples.title: Linked-list helper library
examples.summary: @OnchainLibrary for the linked-list pattern. Companion to LinkedListValidator. Note: uses raw PlutusData throughout — advanced pattern, not the recommended idiom for new code.

examples.name: SwapOrder
examples.title: Atomic swap order
examples.summary: Atomic swap between two parties with redeemer-driven cancel/execute paths.

examples.name: CollateralLoan
examples.title: Collateralized lending
examples.summary: Lending validator with collateral, loan, and liquidation paths.

examples.name: UVerifyV1
examples.title: UVerify protocol — main validator
examples.summary: Main validator of the UVerify protocol (multi-script content verification). Real-world reference; uses proxy + fee pot pattern.

examples.name: UVerifyProxy
examples.title: UVerify upgradeable proxy
examples.summary: Proxy validator delegating to a versioned logic script. Pattern for upgradeable on-chain logic.

examples.name: UVerifyFeePot
examples.title: UVerify fee collection
examples.summary: Fee accumulator validator for the UVerify protocol.

examples.name: UVerifyTxLib
examples.title: UVerify shared on-chain helpers
examples.summary: @OnchainLibrary used by all UVerify scripts.

examples.title: Cardano Foundation: Atomic transaction (multi-validator)
examples.summary: Combined multi-validator demonstrating Cardano's native atomicity: a minting policy requires a secret password while the spending validator always succeeds. If the mint fails the whole transaction fails. Demonstrates @MultiValidator with multiple @Entrypoint(purpose=...) methods.
